COSMIC CONQUEST — THE SPINE

The canonical reference for everything on main: every campaign in play order, every tower, denizen, commander, boon, element, reaction and ability, each with its stable ref and the exact source line it is generated from. Rebuilt from the game itself on every push to main, so it can never describe a version that no longer exists. Pick a power and read its campaign, its arsenal and its army on one sheet.

HUMANITYEleven months ago they told us the date we would die, and everything else in the same breath. Today the rock is gravel, GALACTIC FEDERATION OF LIGHTStand between life and what hunts it, and never rule what you protect. We have kept the first half for nine hundred year THE XENOFor an age the Hungry took consciousness where it grew, and then the Federation drew a line and called it protection. We THE PIRATESEvery power out here drew a border and then needed somebody to carry things across it. That is us. How to reference anything here

Every card on every page carries a mono line: its ref, then the source it is generated from, linked to the exact line on GitHub. Quote the ref in a note ("tower:flak feels weak", "human/intro/slide7 reads flat") and it resolves mechanically: spine.json maps every ref to its page anchor and its source location, for people and for the AI working on the game.

REFtower:flaka tower, on its power's page under THE ARSENAL
REFunit:troopera sendable denizen, under WHAT YOU FIELD
REFcommander:vantaa commander, under WHO LEADS
REFboon:h_refita war boon, under WAR BOONS
REFvigil:shardlinga Vigil machine, on this page
REFcampaign:sol/earth/long-islanda location in the reworked campaign; campaign:sol/earth is its planet, campaign:sol its act, bonus:mercury a parked body
REFhuman/world/MARSthe world text for one power on one planet, five beats and their plates, filed under that planet in THE CAMPAIGN; human/act-text/sol is the act framing written for the five-system galaxy
REFhuman/intro/slide7one slide of a power's opening cinematic
REFhuman/beat3one beat of a power's story spine; human/voice/seat is an alternate voice
REFelement:fire · reaction:thermal · ability:overclock · doctrine:light · playermod:sappers · timeline:12the shared systems, below on this page
REFmap:spine · scenario:assault · arena:swift · target:first · waveroll:r_dmg · lorecodex:patternboards, scenarios, arena modifiers, targeting, wave rolls and the lore codex, below

Canon this page does not render (mythos operations, visual briefs, world generation, arena modifiers, scenarios, maps) lives under those keys in js/lore.js, the frozen lore bible. The pages and spine.json are regenerated together by tools/storyboard.js; tools/gate.js fails if they go stale, and the deploy workflow rebuilds them on every push to main, so only what is actually on main can appear here.

The baseline commander

Unaligned, free, and issued to every profile. The factioned rosters live on their power's own page.

⌂ CADREThe Baseline
No doctrine, no appetite, no vow. Cadre was trained to hold a line with whatever is to hand, and does exactly that: every structure a little better, nothing spectacular. Most commanders are a bet. Cadre is the house.EVEN FOOTING: Every tower gains +6% damage, +6% rate and +6% range, and reanimated attackers are 10% weaker.Interoperability instructor and first field commanderWants: Keep the node alive long enough for the player to learn what every other doctrine costs.Breaks on: Cadre has no ideology of its own and fears becoming only the sum of other people's wars.Standard engagement doctrine. Hold the line and go home.
ABILITIES AND TECH: 2 abilities, 9 tech nodes
  • ⌂ STEADY AIM An even lift across the whole board: +30% damage, +30% rate, +15% range for 8s. (32s cooldown, 8s)
  • ⧗ ATTRITION FIELD Reanimated attackers specifically are gutted: 45% weaker and 30% slower for 9s. (38s cooldown, 9s)
  • DRILL ORDER +5% damage and +5% rate.
  • STANDING ORDERS +7% more of both.
  • GENERAL ORDERS +9% more of both, and +6% range.
  • SIGHTLINES +7% range.
  • SUPPLY +12% kill gold.
  • DEPOT +16% more kill gold and upgrades 10% cheaper.
  • DIG IN +3 maximum lives.
  • HOLDFAST +5 more lives, and reanimates 10% weaker again.
  • THE LINE +7 more lives, and reanimates 15% weaker again.

The campaign: three acts, 18 planets, 63 locations

The reworked campaign (owner directive, docs/CAMPAIGN-REWORK.md): act → planet → location, the last location of a planet being its planetary battle. Every power plays all three acts in its own order and opens at home. 33 locations have a live board, 30 are scheduled to be built. The structure is data on main (js/campaign2.js, gated by probe-campaign2) and is not yet wired into the engine, which still plays the five-system galaxy. The story text written for that galaxy is filed under the matching planets and acts on each power's page.

BOARD TO AUTHORteachingNorthrop Grumman ran its defence programs here for a century. The board catalogue, 35 handcrafted boards

Every planet board, built by hand from the body's real physical character (the italic line under each), filed under the location that fights on it. The chips are the terrain codex: class, flow, cover, barriers, sight, closed vocabularies that double as the brief for future procedural families. The campaign section above is the structure; this is the per-board detail, one card per board. Contested worlds fight on the shared tri boards instead.

The lore codex, 13 entries

The in-game Field Manual's lore pages, word for word.

What The Files Agreed OnThe Disclosure did not release one file. It released decades of them, and every agency had reached the same place without comparing notes first. A Bureau case opened in 1947 stayed open for thirty years and was never closed, only shelved. Navy operators filed the same "round, cold object" against the same abrupt turns, call after call, under a report form named for the range it kept fouling. A French defence institute reached the identical conclusion in 1999 and was thanked and ignored. Nobody needed to be told twice. They had all already written it down.lorecodex:pattern · js/factions.js:1027
September 11, 2028The Disclosure was one broadcast with two announcements in it: that the asteroid Apophis would strike Earth, and everything else. The recovered craft. The programs. The harvest. The edits made to human genetics and to human history. The galaxy’s real order, and where humanity stood in it, which was nowhere. Panic lasted weeks. What settled in after it was stranger: acceptance, and inside the acceptance, people who wanted to fight.lorecodex:disclosure · js/factions.js:1035
The Concord, Holidays 2028Every nation, one conspiracy. While families gathered for what felt like a last holiday season, the disclosed technology and the best minds alive were pooled into two projects: the intercept, and the fleet. Assembling the whole picture taught the planners what the galaxy never said aloud: humanity would never be treated as an equal until its presence was too large and too permanent to deny.lorecodex:concord · js/factions.js:1042
April 13, 2029A Friday. Apophis broke against the intercept, and Earth celebrated, and inside the celebration the hard thing surfaced again: there is always another rock, and there are always beings who call themselves gods. The fleet built to save the planet did not stand down. It departed. The campaign begins on this day, from Earth, and the first system on the map is our own.lorecodex:intercept · js/factions.js:1049
The Old OrderNothing out there is empty. The Federation of Light rings worlds it claims to protect. The Hungry farm worlds they claim to preserve, and humanity was one of their herds. The Pirates hold the roads between, owned by no one and indispensable to everyone. Above all of it stand the Vigil, automatons of a civilization no living power has ever met. Every world you will fight on already belongs to one of them.lorecodex:order · js/factions.js:1055
Five Ways To Take A WorldEvery banner conquers, and none of them conquer alike. Humanity SETTLES: presence that cannot be erased again. The Federation RINGS: defence around a world it will not rule. The Hungry HARVEST: bodies, ground, and consciousness into the yield. The Pirates ROUTE: access, salvage, sanctuary, movement. The Vigil CONTINUES: the standing tasks, executed without a living author. One world can carry all five claims at once.lorecodex:verbs · js/factions.js:1062
The VigilThe Vigil is not a sixth power. Old Weather routines that never stopped running, attached to no living author and deciding nothing: it does not read flags, and it comes down the same corridor at both commanders in the same numbers. Nothing out there is fighting for you.lorecodex:vigil · js/factions.js:1069
The AncientsOlder than the Federation, older than the Hungry, and gone in a way that is not dying: the Ancients shed physical form entirely. A mind that is everywhere has no location, no enemy, and no mouth, and a mind with no mouth issues no commands. Which is the whole mystery of the Vigil: whatever is signing its hostile orders, it is not the silence that built it.lorecodex:ancients · js/factions.js:1074
Who Is Actually Standing ThereThe banner on a world names its claim. The garrison is who fights you for it: a seat fields its commander, a fortress fields its holder’s best, a contested world seats two rivals at once, a Vigil nest fields the machines, and a renegade world fields a splinter of your own power that has stopped answering the order that raised it. Read the briefing before the drop: it names the garrison, not just the flag.lorecodex:garrisons · js/factions.js:1080
Echo ReversalA destroyed hostile leaves a combat-state record that holds for a few seconds. The node reads it, builds an unstable echo, and walks that echo up your own lane, across the neutral ground, into your rival’s defences. Broken a second time, an echo cannot be rebuilt. Every commander answers the protocol differently: a rite may change the shape a kill returns in, never its mass, and two of the five doctrines take nothing off the lane at all.lorecodex:reanimation · js/factions.js:1087
Stars Are Claim StabilityWinning on a world takes it. Winning CLEANLY, three stars, conquers it: the claim holds when you leave, the world’s denizens can join your muster vault, and a fully conquered system pays its bounty and brings its commander out to meet you. Anything less than three stars is a raid the map will remember differently.lorecodex:stars · js/factions.js:1095
SOULSThe harvest currency. Consciousness leaves a signature, the signature can be banked, and the Hungry built an economy on exactly that long before humanity named it. SOULS buy commanders, second abilities, and arsenal permanently, across every campaign on the profile. Stars pay them, conquest pays them, and spending them is the one purchase the galaxy cannot repossess.lorecodex:souls · js/factions.js:1101
ConquestA campaign is five systems, opening in your banner’s own home system. Take worlds, conquer them clean, and the system’s commander comes out to hold their seat. Break all five seats and the galaxy is yours, and the campaign asks its real question: every banner has a public mission and a buried crisis, and the beats between systems are where the crisis surfaces. Claiming a conquered galaxy rolls the next one a tier harder.lorecodex:conquest · js/factions.js:1108

The timeline, 69 events

The canon record, oldest first, from the frozen lore bible (js/lore.js, release 0.5.0). Ref any row as timeline:N.

c. 6.4 million BCEEarliest recoverable Source-Lattice engineering epoch.
Interstellar distance, identity, memory, and coordination make shared infrastructure strategically valuable.		1
c. 930,000-810,000 BCEThe Severance Crisis fractures Lattice access.
Competing political and legal systems attempt incompatible control, isolation, or continuity measures.		2
c. 760,000 BCEAncestor extraction treaties form.
Severed civilizations externalize the cost of lost Lattice functions onto dependent living systems.		3
c. 520,000 BCESol catalogued as a Lattice-adjacent high-diversity biosphere.
Biosphere diversity, Machine stewardship, resources, and gate geography make Sol useful without making it uniquely chosen.		4
9600-8200 BCEGobekli Tepe monumental structures built by hunter-gatherer communities.
Demonstrates early Human organizational and architectural sophistication without requiring nonhuman builders.		5
3rd-1st c. BCEEnochic Watcher traditions develop forbidden-knowledge and angelic-descent themes.
Provides a historical religious source layer later reinterpreted through alien-contact frameworks.		6
late 2nd c. BCEAntikythera Mechanism demonstrates sophisticated Greek astronomical computation.
Ancient technical surprise becomes an evidentiary control against automatic alien attribution.		7
2nd-3rd c. CEGnostic Archon traditions circulate.
Ancient religious rulers later become literalized by modern alien-control interpretations.		8
1803Utsuro-bune legend recorded in Edo-period sources.
Premodern communication-failure story later reread through UFO vocabulary.		9
1882Oahspe published as automatic-writing cosmic revelation.
Shows elaborate heavenly bureaucracy predates modern flying-saucer contactee culture.		10
1896-1897American mystery-airship wave.
Witnesses interpret anomalies using contemporary technological vocabulary.		11
1944-1945Allied aircrews report foo fighters.
Wartime aerial uncertainty creates a recurring modern anomaly template.		12
1946Ghost-rocket wave in Scandinavia.
Unknowns are interpreted through captured German rocket and Soviet threat models.		13
1947Flying-saucer era begins; Roswell retrieval mythology follows.
Public anomaly vocabulary standardizes just as Cold War secrecy expands.		14
1947-2034Calibration Era
Dense calibrated sensing removes many easy anomalies, increasing the value of high-quality residuals.		15
1948-1949Project Sign and Project Grudge.
Formal government investigation produces mixed-quality archives and unresolved residue.		16
1952Project Blue Book and early Ashtar contactee traditions grow in separate source lineages.
Official investigation and UFO religion coexist without validating each other.		17
1954Watcher Mesh Standard
Synthetic media and incompatible exports force native-master and transformation-chain provenance.		18
1955-1960Electrogravitics research is pursued openly by several aerospace firms, then vanishes from the public literature.
The open phase is documented and the silence afterward is real. Whether the silence means cancellation or classification is exactly the kind of gap this setting is built in.		19
1959Project Horizon and Air Force lunar research studies.
Real extreme Cold War planning later supplies texture to secret-space mythology.		20
1960Bracewell proposes autonomous interstellar messenger probes.
Scientific basis for artifact SETI and long-lived autonomous probes.		21
December 1960Brookings delivers its NASA-commissioned study of the social implications of peaceful space activity, including possible extraterrestrial life or artifacts.
Spaceflight made discovery-impact questions legitimate subjects for planning before any discovery existed.		22 · historical-anchor
1960Candidate Zero
Independent sensors image a manufactured object with no known launch provenance; silence prevents immediate attribution.		23
February 3, 1961Strategic Air Command begins continuous Looking Glass airborne command-post operations.
Nuclear command required survivable continuity if ground command centers were destroyed.		24 · historical-anchor
1962Operation Northwoods proposals and Starfish Prime occur in the same year.
Real false-pretext planning and real space-environment alteration demonstrate why proposal, operation, and effect must be separated.		25
1966Signal Winter
High-profile false positives and synthetic evidence collapse public confidence; serious anomaly work moves behind restricted programs.		26
October 1969 / report filed 1973Jimmy Carter reports an unidentified light seen near Leary, Georgia; the report later enters presidential-library holdings.
A high-status witness converts an ordinary unresolved-observation problem into a durable public-disclosure reference point.		27 · historical-anchor
1970Vasin and Shcherbakov publish the speculative artificial-Moon / spaceship-Moon hypothesis.
Apollo-era lunar discoveries create a receptive environment for technological reinterpretation of lunar anomalies.		28 · source-history
1972Pellegrino Ernetti publicly advances the Chronovisor claim.
Time-viewing, electronic voice, religious history, and Cold War technology merge into a modern retrocognition legend.		29 · source-history
1972Open-Sky Hungry
No single government can monopolize Solar observations, so rival polities agree on minimum metadata standards.		30
1974Arecibo Message; modern scripture-engineering and pseudo-ancient aviation debates.
Human outreach and mythic engineering reinterpretation become parallel source traditions.		31
1976Tehran incident; Sitchin and Sirius ancient-contact reinterpretations published.
Authentic case and fringe source lineages become easy to collapse online unless evidence labels remain visible.		32
1976Phase-Correlation Experiments
Multi-lab work isolates a weak consciousness-linked instrument residual without validating old paranormal systems.		33
1977Vrillon intrusion and Alternative 3 broadcast.
Broadcast, fiction, and contactee language create durable source-contamination patterns.		34
1980Noetic Authentication
The residual becomes a reproducible identity-continuity channel.		35
1981-1984Law of One / Ra sessions.
Provides fictional design concepts for free will, Orion, social memory, and quarantine without becoming verified history.		36
1981-2017Saturn's north polar hexagon is observed by Voyager and then tracked for decades by Cassini: a persistent six-sided jet stream roughly thirty thousand kilometres across that does not drift.
A genuinely unexplained regular polygon at planetary scale. Nothing else in the solar system has corners, which is why this fiction puts the door there.		37
1984Abyssal Reply
Old Weather returns a valid authentication response but no interpretable political message.		38
1985Far Journeys publishes Loosh narrative.
Later consciousness-farm lore merges it with unrelated alien traditions.		39
September 21, 1987Ronald Reagan tells the UN that a hypothetical alien threat might make human commonality obvious.
A rhetorical device about global unity later becomes detached from context and recycled in disclosure and false-flag narratives.		40 · historical-anchor
1987Handshake at L5
Candidate Zero answers with permissions, versioning, and revoked-authority metadata.		41
1992Artifact Consensus
Independent replication establishes a non-Human technological system predating current spaceflight.		42
1997Solar Sovereignty Crisis
Off-world Human polities refuse Earth-wide authority over contact and artifacts.		43
2002First Contact Mandate fails
No Human government gains accepted authority to control nonhuman infrastructure; unsanctioned expeditions accelerate.		44
2004Nimitz/Tic Tac incident.
Multi-source case strengthens Human sensor-chain methodology.		45
2008Planet Nine and Sol Anchor
A natural distant planet is found; a separate artificial installation is identified nearby.		46
2010Anchor Crisis
Humans and Old Weather disagree over salvage, custody, and successor rights.		47
2014Sol Gate opens
Rival Human blocs activate the Gate before species-wide political consensus exists.		48
March 8, 2014Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 disappears with 239 aboard and is never recovered.
The disappearance itself is documented fact. A later recording purporting to show three luminous objects circling the aircraft in formation before a flash is widely assessed as fabricated, and is carried here as a CONTESTED ARTIFACT rather than evidence. Its value to this fiction is the shape of the claim: objects in a ring, then absence.		49
2015First Gate Diaspora
Unapproved expeditions recover mixed-origin salvage, explaining rapid pre-contact technology blending.		50
2017Oumuamua becomes first confirmed interstellar object.
Proves extrasolar material naturally crosses the Solar System.		51
2017Living Contact
Humans meet refugees, traders, defectors, and post-imperial communities rather than one monolithic alien civilization.		52
2018Treaty Mirror
Hungry-aligned brokers privately approach Human institutions through contradictory identities and legacy claims.		53
2019Authenticated Federation Contact
The Galactic Federation of Light becomes the first living nonhuman polity to pass planetary-scale Human provenance tests.		54
2021Disclosure Fracture
Human, Federation, Hungry, Pirate, and Machine archives contradict one another, turning history into active politics.		55
2022Ashtar Declaration
Ashtar voids historic Hungry claims and offers protection/Federation, triggering the Human consent crisis.		56
2023-02High-altitude object detections surge after radar scrutiny changes.
Detection policy itself changes the anomaly population.		57
2023-07/09Congressional UAP hearing and NASA independent study.
Public allegations and scientific data-quality standards become competing disclosure narratives.		58
2023Client Awakening
Dormant Hungry dependencies activate across legal, genetic, economic, religious, and technical systems.		59
2024AARO historical report.
Official review documents claim history while reporting no verified hidden extraterrestrial reverse-engineering evidence.		60
2024Farm Revolts
Liberation reveals client populations may biologically or infrastructurally depend on the systems being dismantled.		61
20253I/ATLAS identified as third known interstellar object.
Provides a natural interstellar control case.		62
2025Sol Protective Quarantine
Federation transit restrictions block renewed extraction but are perceived by Humans as external rule.		63
2026UAP archives and public provenance databases expand.
Versioned records make later Archive War analysis possible.		64
2027Scrap Constellation Charter
Smugglers, refugee fleets, route pilots, and sanctuary ports become a coherent nonterritorial Pirate polity.		65
2028Weather Seed / Vigil Declaration
Machine mission spreads beyond Sol and divergent copies demand political personhood while Vigil routines remain neutral.		66
2029-04-13Apophis is intercepted and broken. The rock is hollow and crewed: a delivery vehicle of Hungry stock and maker-format units, which the intercept scatters intact across half a planet instead of burning on entry. The Federation of Light had ruled the object a natural event and declined to divert it, and so never looked inside it.
The public record of a safe pass is preserved as the cover story; the timing residual is the tell.		67
2029Five-Way War
All five conquest systems become simultaneously scalable across reactivated Source-Lattice pentads.		68
2029The hexagon is entered and found to be an aperture: six emitters held in circular phase, twisting local spacetime until separation across the opening falls to zero.
Reverse engineering it shows the principle is general and the scale is not fixed. A ring of oscillators spun up in formation opens a seamless passage for as long as it is held, which is the mechanism the contested 2014 artifact appears to describe in miniature.		69

The relationship web, 19 threads

Every authored tension between commanders, from the lore bible. Ref a thread as rel:a-b.

DIR. REYES & CANTORArchive versus narrative
Vanta distrusts persuasive coherence without provenance; Cantor thinks raw records can be weaponized by withholding interpretation.		rel:vanta-cantor
GEN. OKAFOR & DREGGLogistics versus monopoly
Both understand supply better than ideology. Korrin builds public standards; Dregg makes scarcity personally profitable.		rel:korrin-dregg
GEN. OKAFOR & DREGG-RThe auditable war
The Audit proves Korrin's systems also create dependency, forcing Humanity to defend the difference between standardization and capture.		rel:korrin-dregg_r
DR. TANAKA & NYX-ROriginal and correction
Nyx sees the Mirror Trial as theft of risk she personally survived; NYX-R sees itself as the first version allowed to learn from her consequences.		rel:nyx-nyx_r
CHF. O'RYAN & AXIOMMaker and person
Orin wants to repair Axiom; Axiom wants him to admit repair is a negotiation with a citizen.		rel:orin-axiom
MAR. WASHINGTON & HALDERSovereignty versus rescue
Both defend vulnerable populations. Vess will accept deaths rather than external rule; Halder will impose temporary safety rather than permit extinction.		rel:vess-halder
SERAPH & SEVRAConsent versus inherited obligation
Seraph treats identity as a present agreement; Sevra treats obligation as an asset that survives death.		rel:seraph-sevra
AURELIA & SEVRACare versus continuity brokerage
Both preserve the dead. Aurelia restores personhood; Sevra preserves utility and contract.		rel:aurelia-sevra
LUMEN & LUMEN-RAuthority versus earned trust
Lumen inherits lawful ward credentials; LUMEN-R begins untrusted and becomes secure through evidence.		rel:lumen-lumen_r
CANTOR & THRAXPersuasion versus absorption
Cantor wants disagreement to remain audible; Thrax treats disagreement as an internal process of one larger self.		rel:cantor-thrax
HALDER & RAKECordon versus corridor
Halder closes routes to protect populations; Rake opens them because protection without escape becomes custody.		rel:halder-rake
MAWLORD & MAWLORD-RHunger versus learned optimization
Mawlord claims appetite is biology and liberation. The Starved Set demonstrates predation can be learned from the battlefield itself.		rel:mawlord-mawlord_r
ULGRIM & SERAPHSingular value versus universal dignity
Ulgrim values rare minds more than common bodies; Seraph insists dignity is not a scarcity market.		rel:ulgrim-seraph
RAKE & DREGGNetwork versus throne
Rake wants routes no one owns. Dregg wants the Pirate network to admit it already functions as his state.		rel:rake-dregg
SCARLET & HALDERLiberation versus containment
Scarlet destroys cordons before asking why they exist; Halder accepts being hated if the threat is real.		rel:scarlet-halder
GRIST & CHF. O'RYANSalvage versus stewardship
Both make wreckage useful. Orin asks whether the object can be repaired; Grist asks whether anyone can still enforce ownership.		rel:grist-orin
CINDER & LUMENDenial versus preservation
Cinder destroys compromised systems; Lumen protects their authentic core and accepts the cost of careful recovery.		rel:cinder-lumen
DREGG & DREGG-RLegend versus ledger
Dregg treats charisma as a strategic asset. The Audit records every hidden subsidy beneath his myth of independence.		rel:dregg-dregg_r
AXIOM & THRAXVigil persons versus coercive collective
Axiom argues that copies may diverge freely. Thrax argues that divergence should be reconciled inside one mind.		rel:axiom-thrax
